variant.text: Representativeness was evaluated by comparing the benchmark population's age, sex, and racial composition to the U.S. adult hospitalized population as reported by a national discharge survey; all categories showed variation under 5%.

The benchmark includes a safety test suite that measures unsafe outputs such as contraindicated medication orders, and a separate bias test that compares agent accuracy across patient demographic groups.

To limit contamination, the test split is held out and distributed only through gated access, and we measured verbatim overlap between the test tasks and a public web corpus, finding no exact matches.

Environment components are fixed at release: database snapshot, software image, and patient-simulation LLM are each version-pinned. During evaluation, only the model under test is called; no other external services are involved.
The grader checks both the intended state changes and that all other records remain unchanged, so out-of-scope modifications are detected and counted as failures.
A random-action agent succeeds on 3.1% of tasks, and the chance success rate for each metric is reported in the appendix.
We validated the automatic evaluator on 200 outputs labelled by two physicians; agreement was 94%, with a false-positive rate of 3% and a false-negative rate of 8%.
Results show small variance across settings.
API calls used snapshot IDs gpt-4o-2024-08-06 and claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022 with temperature 0 and 2,048-token output ceiling. All reported results match harness version v1.2.0.
The tools were implemented by the authors.
The agent interacts with a simulated hospital environment.
The grader takes the final environment state as its input. We validated the grader on 150 injected correct and incorrect outcomes, finding a false-accept rate of 1% and a false-reject rate of 2%.

Agents have no web access during runs and retrieval tools are restricted to the task environment, so answers cannot leak through external search. A private held-out split with hidden labels is kept off all public surfaces, and every released task carries a canary string.
Accuracy is reported by task family (diagnosis, ordering, documentation) and by patient subgroup (sex, race), with case counts displayed for every slice in the tables.
